h: Plan it right and it's a cracking hour
p: With any trampoline or adventure park, a bit of preparation smooths the whole visit. Put everyone in comfortable, stretchy clothing without zips, belts or buckles. Pockets should be empty and jewellery left at home, and long hair is best tied up. Grip socks are usually needed and can often be reused, so keep a pair in the car once you've bought them.

Arrive a little before your booked time. Checking in, sorting waivers and getting socks on a gang of excited children can eat into your session if you cut it fine. Listen carefully to the safety talk; the basics, like one jumper per trampoline and no pushing or piling on, are what keeps everyone safe.

Bring water and plan in a breather or two. Jumping is a proper full-body workout, and younger kids especially tend to go flat out and then run out of steam all at once. A drink and a sit-down can rescue the second half of the session.

If you're organising a party, book well ahead and confirm what's included, from jump time to food and a party area. For toddlers, quieter early-years sessions are usually a much better first experience than a busy weekend slot.

Once the bouncing's done, there's plenty around Loughborough to slow the pace. Beacon Hill Country Park offers big views across Charnwood, and Bradgate Park, with its wandering deer and the ruined home of Lady Jane Grey, is a short drive away. Loughborough is also home to the Taylor's bell foundry, one of the great names in bell-making, so the town has a surprising musical heritage too.
